title: Inference deployment sell scripts and canary checklist (Draft v2)
content:
Purpose:
Short working doc for field sellers and solutions engineers to: 1) pick the right deployment recommendation (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) quickly, 2) run a safe canary/rollout and know rollback triggers, and 3) have tight, testable objection-response scripts for pricing and reliability questions. This is intentionally a compact one-pager + speaker notes for calls.

Quick decision rubric (cheat sheet):
- Hosted API: recommend when customer wants fastest time-to-value, minimal ops, or low early volume. Signal words: 'PoC', 'start small', 'unknown throughput'. Pricing move: emphasize free credits + meterable per-token billing.
- Dedicated: recommend when predictable throughput, steady production traffic, data isolation, or cost predictability is required. Signal words: 'commit', 'SLA', 'throughput guarantee', 'burst capacity'.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): recommend when regulatory controls, strict data residency, or air-gapped compliance is non-negotiable. Signal words: 'HIPAA', 'SOC2/PCI restrictions', 'no external network'.

Conversation opener (30–60s):
- SE: "Quick orientation — are you building something experimental or pushing to production? That tells us whether we start on Hosted or jump to Dedicated/Private."
- Follow-ups: "What’s the 95th percentile latency that would make the UI feel choppy for your customers? And do you have a firm monthly token budget or is it flexible?"

Three short pitch bullets for each deployment (speaker notes):
- Hosted: "Lowest friction to iterate; we handle kernel selection, autoscaling, and routing. Great for early UX testing and biz-metric validation. If you hit predictable spend we can plan a Dedicated migration path."
- Dedicated: "Reserved GPU pools with SLAs, consistent throughput and predictable unit economics. Configurable autoscale and burst rules so you can handle batch jobs + steady traffic in one contract."
- Private: "Full control over network and keys, integrations for enterprise KMS/HSM, and audit logs for compliance teams — plus the same Redwood runtime API so dev experience is consistent."

Objection-response snippets (copyable lines):
- "Latency concerns": "We can run a short latency baseline during your POC with a similar request profile; if p95 is > target we have knobbed options (quantized variants, routing to lower-latency model variant, or Dedicated pins) and an SLA-backed path to reduce variance."
- "Cost pushback": "We provide transparent per-route token cost breakdowns and Optimize recommendations — simple levers like caching prefixes or switching to a quantized variant often reduce cost by 20–40% without degrading user experience. We can baseline expected monthly token spend with a small sample set in <2 weeks."
- "We already have infra": "Totally — Redwood's Private deploy fits into existing VPCs and can run alongside your infra. The value is in not having to rewrite serving/kv-cache code and in predictable unit economics and operational tooling (rollouts/tracing)."

Negotiation anchors (language to use):
- Start: "Our standard Dedicated package for your expected throughput would be $X/mo with a 12-month commit — that gives you reserved capacity, burst buffers, and an SLA. We can pilot host traffic on Hosted for 30 days and convert usage to a credit against the first Dedicated month if you commit within the pilot window."
- Concession play: "If budget is the blocker, propose a time-bound pilot with reduced commit (6 months) + a defined uplift to full committed capacity at month 6. Include a migration support credit in the SOW."

Canary & rollout checklist (field-friendly, copy into pre-call notes):
- Pre-canary requirements:
  - Define success metrics: latency p95 target, error rate threshold, request throughput baseline, business metric (e.g., CTR/click-to-response).
  - Instrumentation: ensure Console tracing enabled and token-level cost breakdown; add synthetic monitors for endpoints.
  - Dataset: prepare a sampled request set (1000–5000 requests) representative of production distribution.
- Canary run (day 0–7):
  - Traffic split: start at 1% production traffic -> observe for 24h -> 5% -> 24h -> 20% -> 72h.
  - Monitoring checklist: p50/p95 latency, p99 tail spikes, 5xx error rates, token spend per request, user-facing error counts.
  - Rollforward criteria: stable p95 within target for 48h and no correlated spike in 5xx or cost > 2x forecast for same period.
  - Rollback triggers (explicit): sustained p95 > target for 2 measurement windows, sudden 5xx increase > 3x baseline, or business KPI drop > 5% week-over-week during canary.
- Post-canary: formalize runbook, save KV cache/quantization config used, PR to infra repo with rollout notes (link in linked_artifacts), and schedule a 1-week check-in with SRE/Customer Success.

Metric thresholds (examples for field use — adapt by customer):
- interactive UI use-case: p95 < 350ms (in-region), p99 < 700ms, 5xx < 0.1%
- background batch inference: throughput target >= 300 tokens/sec per GPU (depends on model & quantization), cost per 1M tokens < $Y (estimate during proposal)

Technical detours sellers should know (soundbites):
- "Composable routing": we can route by latency/cost/region and fallback automatically to a cheaper variant when load spikes — so you can guarantee SLAs at the application level.
- "KV cache and prefix caching": large savings for conversational workloads where history re-use is common — mention as a quick Optimize win.

Sample objection: "We tried model quantization before and saw quality regressions."
- Response: "We run A/B comparisons on your prompt set and provide a QA pass with human evals across key prompts. Quantization is suggested by Redwood Optimize only when regressions are within an acceptable tolerance or when the quality delta is measurable and reversible during rollout."

Pre-call template for AE/SE (copy into calendar invite):
- Goals: (1) confirm production vs POC, (2) identify regulatory constraints, (3) agree signal test set and success metrics for a 2-week pilot.
- Required attendees: AE, SE, customer infra/SRE, decision maker for budget/compliance.
- Artifacts to bring: sample prompt set, expected qps, current cost baseline (if any).

Open TODOs (short):

- [SE] Create a 1-click canary dashboard template in Console for AE demos (GH PR 56 reference) — Maya
- [GTM] One-pager: "What counts as a rollback" with examples and language for contract SOWs — Jordan

Notes to self:
- Keep this doc small and field-friendly — long engineering docs live on Confluence.
- Next iteration: add 2–3 customer-specific micro-scripts (SaaS search, customer support summarization, internal assistant) based on top target segments.

Quick references / links:
- Confluence playbook: CONFLUENCE-7890
- Pilot SOW template: https://docs.redwood.example/pilot-sow-template (internal)
- Jira epic for canary dashboard work: JIRA-4321

End of draft v2. Feedback welcome — planning to iterate after next AE shadowing sessions.
